sections.title: What are Shortest Path Algorithms?
sections.content:
Shortest path in an **unweighted** graph is BFS — each edge has cost 1. Add weights and BFS fails: a path with more hops can be shorter if those hops have tiny weights.

**Dijkstra's algorithm**: O((V+E) log V) with a priority queue. Greedy — always extend the cheapest known path next. Works only with non-negative weights. Used in navigation systems, network routing, game pathfinding.

**Bellman-Ford**: O(VE). Handles negative weights by relaxing all edges V-1 times. An extra pass detects negative cycles.

**Floyd-Warshall**: O(V³). Computes all-pairs shortest paths. Practical only for small V (≤ ~500).

Choose by: non-negative weights + single source → Dijkstra. Negative weights or cycle detection → Bellman-Ford. All pairs + small graph → Floyd-Warshall. Unweighted → BFS.

sections.title: When to Use This
sections.content: Dijkstra for single-source shortest path with non-negative weights. Bellman-Ford when negative weights are present or you need to detect negative cycles. Floyd-Warshall for all-pairs distances on small graphs. BFS remains correct for unweighted graphs.

sections.title: Dijkstra, Bellman-Ford, and Floyd-Warshall
sections.content:
## Dijkstra's Algorithm

Invariant: when a node is popped from the min-heap, its distance is final. Holds because all edge weights are non-negative.

1. `dist[source]=0`, `dist[others]=Infinity`.
2. Push `(0, source)` to min-heap.
3. Pop `(d, node)`. If `d > dist[node]`, skip — stale entry.
4. For each neighbor: if `dist[node]+w < dist[neighbor]`, update and push.

The stale-entry check is essential because we push updated distances without removing old entries.

## Why Dijkstra Fails on Negative Weights

The invariant breaks — a future negative edge might give a shorter path to an already-settled node. Results are silently wrong.

## Bellman-Ford

For each of V-1 iterations, relax every edge: if `dist[u]+w < dist[v]`, set `dist[v]=dist[u]+w`. Why V-1? Shortest path visits at most V-1 edges.

Negative cycle detection: run a Vth iteration. If any distance still updates, a negative cycle is reachable.

## Floyd-Warshall

`dp[i][j] = min(dp[i][j], dp[i][k] + dp[k][j])` for each intermediate k. Init: `dp[i][i]=0`, direct edge weights, Infinity otherwise. O(V³).

## K-Constrained Paths

Run exactly K iterations of Bellman-Ford for shortest paths using at most K edges. Use a snapshot of dist at the start of each iteration to prevent chaining within one pass.

sections.title: Core Template
sections.explanation: Dijkstra with stale-entry skip for correctness with duplicate heap entries. Bellman-Ford with early exit optimization and negative cycle detection on the Vth pass.

items.name: Dijkstra with K-Step Constraint
items.description: Run K iterations of Bellman-Ford (instead of V-1) for shortest paths using at most K edges. Use a snapshot copy of dist before each iteration to prevent within-pass chaining.

items.name: Modified Dijkstra with Custom Cost
items.description: For problems where cost is max edge weight on the path rather than sum, modify what you minimize and how you update. The heap stores (costSoFar, node) with a custom cost function.

items.name: Floyd-Warshall All-Pairs
items.description: Initialize distance matrix with direct edge weights and Infinity for non-edges. Iterate over all k as intermediate nodes. Detects negative cycles if dp[i][i] < 0 after completion.

sections.title: Complexity
sections.time: Dijkstra: O((V+E) log V) | Bellman-Ford: O(VE) | Floyd-Warshall: O(V³)
sections.space: Dijkstra: O(V+E) | Bellman-Ford: O(V) | Floyd-Warshall: O(V²)
sections.explanation: Dijkstra: each vertex popped once (O(V log V)) and each edge triggers at most one heap push (O(E log V)). Bellman-Ford: V-1 iterations over all E edges. Floyd-Warshall: three nested loops over V nodes. Space is dominated by the data structure: adjacency list O(V+E), distance array O(V), or matrix O(V²).

sections.title: Common Mistakes
items: Using Dijkstra with negative weights — it gives silently wrong answers. The invariant that a popped node has its final distance breaks with negative edges.
Forgetting the stale-entry check in Dijkstra — without 'if d > dist[node] continue', stale heap entries cause nodes to be reprocessed with outdated distances.
Bellman-Ford K-step variant: not copying dist before each iteration — relaxations within one pass can chain beyond K edges. Use a snapshot of dist at iteration start.
Floyd-Warshall: initializing non-existent edges to 0 instead of Infinity — this implies free edges exist and corrupts all-pairs distances.
Not running the Vth Bellman-Ford iteration for negative cycle detection — skipping it returns wrong distances when a negative cycle is reachable from the source.

items.why: Direct Dijkstra — find shortest time for signal to reach all nodes, then take the maximum shortest path.

sections.title: What to Learn Next
sections.why: Union-Find is the data structure behind Kruskal's MST — the natural complement to Dijkstra. Where Dijkstra finds shortest paths, Kruskal finds the cheapest set of edges connecting all nodes. Union-Find's near-O(1) connectivity queries are also useful standalone for dynamic connectivity problems.
